title: Musicians who left for the city: Pierre Anderson and Amos White
summary: Who moved from the country to the city; Pierre Anderson played sousaphone with dance bands including Amos White's.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, I was thinking Harrison and Chris moved here and you moved here. Your brother Sam moved here. Who else moved here and played music? In the city? From down there?
You may see. There must have been some others. You may see. Well, take my son of Henry. He left. He left. Mike Gouldie came in and played.
Who did he play with down there?
He played with Mike Gouldie band. Uh huh. Mike Gouldie band. And uh, Harrison Bones, Pierre Anderson. He left the country and played with all the different bands. Chris Kelly.
Who did Pierre Anderson play with? I don't know about him.
Pierre Anderson played bass with Dick Salsis band. Uh huh. Dick Salsis. He's played with all the bands. Uh huh. He was a good, he was a good Suzaphone player.
He played with all the bands. Did he play in dance orchestras?
What did he play, Suzaphone or string bass?
Oh, Suzaphone. Uh huh. Suzaphone, yeah.
You remember the dance officers that he played with?

Well, I know you like that lick. He played at the, uh, the, uh, what do you call that place? Chancey, Chancey, I think. Chancey, yeah. Chancey, yeah. Chancey, yeah. He played with the, uh, but, uh, but, uh, called Amos White.
He's living out in California today.
Yeah, I see, I, I met Amos in San Francisco. Mm hmm. Yeah, Peer, where the, where the chance is is a long time. Mm hmm. Him and Sonny Henry, Sonny on trombone, Peer on bass. Amos White on trumpet.
